A recurrent state cache cannot be rewound for free because the state is a compressed, non-invertible summary of all previous inputs. Unlike a simple buffer where you can just move a pointer back, the mathematical transformation that updates the state (such as in an LSTM or RNN) is not reversible without storing the entire history of intermediate values. To rewind, the engine must either recompute the state from the beginning of the sequence, which costs time proportional to the sequence length, or maintain a full history of states, which costs memory proportional to the sequence length. There is no zero-cost way to undo the information loss inherent in the recurrent update step.
